primary_lower_bound_reconstruction.title: Formula Caching in DPLL
primary_lower_bound_reconstruction.target_result: Theorem 4.24: any FCWS refutation of GT_n requires at least 2^(n-2) nodes.
witness_mechanism: Restrictions whose unit-propagated residuals induce partial orders.
Lemma 4.23: under Weakening/Subsumption comparability, prune(sigma)=prune(tau) for residuals without units/contradiction.
Novel branch points branch on variables crossing distinct Hasse-diagram components.
At novelty level n-2, at least 2^(n-2) mutually incompatible residual-order states remain.
The lower bound therefore depends on structural distinguishability of residual partial orders, not merely raw node counting.
primary_lower_bound_reconstruction.spider_interpretation: The missing C023 robustness theorem should be tested against the exact prune/novel-branch invariant. Counting local resolvents alone cannot transfer Theorem 4.24. This is a research target description, not an algorithmic recommendation.

critical_fragility_found.finding: GT_n also has polynomial-size regular Resolution refutations, classically O(n^3).
critical_fragility_found.meaning: A polynomially bounded local Resolution rule can in principle destroy an FC/FCWS lower-bound witness even if it derives only polynomially many clauses at each state. Robustness must control what those clauses do to the prune/novel-branch structure.

new_external_routes.need: Extract the exact clause families and dependency depth of the known polynomial regular-resolution refutation P_n for GT_n, so later analysis can ask whether the registered one-layer local pass can realize the witness-destroying steps.

new_external_routes.finding: Modern Tseitin lower bounds connect regular Resolution to DNNF/read-once branching-program representations and obtain exponential lower bounds controlled by treewidth.
new_external_routes.possible_relevance: This supplies mature machinery for C023 Route C/D only if an independently proved simulation maps JANUS-FC_local or a restricted projection of it into the target representation model.

new_external_routes.finding: Formula-caching variants that return reusable reasons are materially stronger than basic Boolean residual caching; FC_reason^W polynomially simulates regular Resolution while basic FC/FCWS does not.
new_external_routes.need: Keep reason existence, reason language, and reason extraction cost separate. Search for the weakest reason interface that is independently checkable and whose discovery cost is explicit.

new_external_routes.finding: Guarded graph tautologies have polynomial pool-resolution / clause-learning proofs under appropriate proof-search structure.
new_external_routes.meaning: Graph-tautology hardness is sensitive to the exact proof system. Any JANUS lower-bound transfer must name the exact rule set and cannot inherit hardness from a nearby weaker system.

new_external_routes.finding: Recent proof-complexity work studies algorithms/refuter problems that locate invalid steps in purported short proofs or analyze proofs of lower-bound statements.
new_external_routes.spider_use: Useful for auditing candidate lower-bound certificates and designing counterexample-oriented review; not a SAT speedup and not a lower-bound theorem for JANUS-FC_local.

new_external_routes.finding: Finding near-shortest Resolution proofs is itself hard in strong formal senses; efficient verification of a short proof must remain separate from efficient discovery.

Search specifically for existing named systems/theorems matching a deterministic one-layer, non-saturating, polynomial-budget local Resolution closure followed by branching and exact residual caching. A direct match would be more valuable than another generic SAT paper.

Continue proof-forensics literature only as SPIDER support: proof analysis, refuters, trace slicing, alignment and certificate bug localization.
